statement: Traditional brands like Hermès, Chanel, and Louis Vuitton impose no mandatory geometric constraints on their patterns, leading to inconsistent visual identity across products and artisans.
evidence: Where The Assumption Breaks, point 2: 'Traditional brands impose no mandatory geometric constraints on their patterns. Two garments from the same brand, made by different artisans, can have different proportions while carrying the same decorative elements.'
